sources.title: Nakai-Moishezon ampleness criterion for real line bundles
sources.finding: All-dimensional positive intersections characterize ampleness on complete schemes over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic. Only the Cartier case is needed.
Trivial inertia identifies the actual algebraic stack as an algebraic space.
Separated locally quasi-finite space over a scheme is representable.
Proper quasi-finite morphisms of schemes are finite.
Proper flat finite-presentation pushforward of a perfect complex is perfect and compatible with arbitrary base change.
The reduced-base direct descent alternative applies after the universal structure-sheaf pushforward condition is established.
Proper connected nodal curve families have universally trivial structure-sheaf pushforward. A smooth P1 family satisfies the hypotheses.
Degree is preserved by birational proper curve maps and multiplied by the full generic degree under a nonconstant proper curve map, with no separability hypothesis.
